title: Nvidia may guarantee $250bn so OpenAI can afford the data centre that will house its chips
excerpt: Nvidia is in talks to provide roughly $250 billion in financing guarantees for OpenAI, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter. The backstop would let OpenAI lease a 10-gigawatt campus in southern Ohio that SoftBank’s energy subsidiary is developing. The reason such a guarantee is needed is straightforward: OpenAI […]
content_html:
Nvidia is in talks to provide roughly $250 billion in financing guarantees for OpenAI, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter. The backstop would let OpenAI lease a 10-gigawatt campus in southern Ohio that SoftBank’s energy subsidiary is developing.

The reason such a guarantee is needed is straightforward: OpenAI does not have an investment-grade credit rating. Nvidia’s balance sheet would effectively stand in for one, letting lenders price the debt against the chipmaker’s credit rather than the borrower’s.

What the money covers

The $250 billion figure applies to the data centre lease and construction debt, not to the Nvidia chips that will fill the building. Those are the subject of a separate discussion, with the Journal reporting chip purchase financing that could reach a further $350 billion.

The whole project is expected to cost more than $500 billion including silicon. Its first phase, around 800 megawatts, is due for completion in 2028.

Nvidia’s backing would support financing vehicles designed to reassure lenders about the project’s funding. Reuters said it could not immediately verify the report, and Nvidia, OpenAI, and the US Commerce Department did not respond to requests for comment.

Why the site is political

The power for the Ohio campus is controlled by the US government and funded separately by Japan under a recent trade deal, tied to Tokyo’s pledge to invest $33 billion in a natural gas plant. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is involved in deciding who gets access.

OpenAI has been in advanced talks for the site for several weeks and is among the keenest bidders. Anthropic, Microsoft, and Google have also approached Lutnick in recent weeks, according to the Journal.

The circularity problem

Michael Burry, the investor known for shorting the housing market before 2008, posted on X: “Around and around we go. Nvidia to guarantee $200 billion of ChatGPT’s spending on $NVDA chips.” He had added to his Nvidia short position on Friday at $210.28.

Tech commentator Ed Zitron was blunter, calling it “such an insane thing to do on so many levels and about as bearish as it gets, especially considering it is being built by SoftBank.” Both were reacting to the same structural feature: a chip supplier underwriting its customer’s ability to keep buying chips.

Nvidia has already committed more than $40 billion to AI equity positions, including roughly $30 billion in OpenAI. Its investment in Ilya Sutskever’s Safe Superintelligence is arguably the purest version of the pattern, in which Nvidia funds companies that then spend the money on Nvidia hardware.

A structure with precedent

Vendor guarantees on data centre obligations are no longer unusual, though the scale here is. Google has guaranteed roughly $44 billion of other companies’ data centre rent, a figure the proposed Nvidia backstop would exceed by nearly six times.

OpenAI’s own capital structure has become increasingly layered. Eight banks are now backing SoftBank’s record $40 billion OpenAI loan, and SoftBank has separately sought margin lending secured against its OpenAI stake.

Much of this obligation sits outside conventional debt disclosure. Research has put Big Tech’s off-balance-sheet AI commitments at around $1.65 trillion, with Meta alone accounting for roughly $420 billion, nearly triple its reported debt.

What OpenAI gets out of it

For OpenAI, the deal would be a first move towards owning its compute rather than renting it from Microsoft, Amazon, and Oracle. Control over infrastructure is the difference between negotiating capacity and dictating it.

For Nvidia, the calculation is demand certainty. Guaranteeing the building locks in years of chip orders from a customer that would otherwise struggle to finance them, which is precisely why critics find the arrangement uncomfortable.

The scale question

AI infrastructure spending is set to exceed $700 billion this year, and the industry is expected to spend more than $3 trillion through 2028 on data centres, much of it financed against the chips inside them. The central risk is not that AI fails to matter, but that the buildout overshoots demand or that returns get competed away faster than the debt amortises.

Nothing has been signed. The Journal noted the talks about the site and its financing remain in progress and subject to change, which for a $250 billion guarantee is a considerable caveat.

content_html_zh:
据《华尔街日报》周日援引知情人士的话报道，英伟达正在洽谈为 OpenAI 提供约 2500 亿美元的融资担保。 该支持计划将允许 OpenAI 在俄亥俄州南部租用软银能源子公司正在开发的 10 吉瓦园区。

需要这样的保证的原因很简单：OpenAI 没有投资级信用评级。 英伟达的资产负债表实际上可以替代这一点，让贷方根据芯片制造商的信用而不是借款人的信用来定价债务。

钱涵盖了什么

2500 亿美元的数字适用于数据中心租赁和建设债务，而不是用于填充该建筑的 Nvidia 芯片。 这些都是单独讨论的主题，据《华尔街日报》报道，芯片购买融资可能进一步达到 3500 亿美元。

包括硅在内，整个项目预计耗资超过 5000 亿美元。 第一阶段发电量约为 800 兆瓦，预计将于 2028 年完工。

英伟达的支持将支持旨在让贷方放心该项目资金的融资工具。 路透社表示无法立即核实该报道，英伟达、OpenAI 和美国商务部也没有回应置评请求。

为什么该网站具有政治性

俄亥俄园区的电力由美国政府控制，并根据最近的一项贸易协议由日本单独提供资金，该协议与东京承诺投资 330 亿美元建设天然气工厂有关。 商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克参与决定谁可以获得访问权。

OpenAI 已经对该网站进行了数周的高级谈判，并且是最热心的竞标者之一。 据《华尔街日报》报道，Anthropic、微软和谷歌最近几周也与卢特尼克进行了接触。

圆度问题

迈克尔·伯里 (Michael Burry) 是一位因 2008 年之前做空房地产市场而闻名的投资者，他在 X 上发帖称：“我们绕来绕去。 Nvidia 将保证 ChatGPT 在 NVDA 芯片上的 2000 亿美元支出。” 周五，他增加了 Nvidia 空头头寸，价格为 210.28 美元。

科技评论员埃德·齐特龙(Ed Zitron)则直言不讳，称其“在如此多的层面上做如此疯狂的事情，而且几乎看跌，尤其是考虑到它是由软银打造的。” 两者都对相同的结构特征做出反应：芯片供应商为其客户提供继续购买芯片的能力。

Nvidia 已承诺投资超过 400 亿美元的 AI 股权，其中包括约 300 亿美元的 OpenAI。 它对 Ilya Sutskever 的 Safe Superintelligence 的投资可以说是该模式最纯粹的版本，其中 Nvidia 资助公司，然后将钱花在 Nvidia 硬件上。

有先例的结构

供应商对数据中心义务的保证已不再罕见，尽管规模如此之大。 谷歌已经保证了其他公司大约 440 亿美元的数据中心租金，而英伟达提出的担保方案将超出这一数字近六倍。

OpenAI自身的资本结构已经变得越来越分层。 目前有八家银行支持软银创纪录的 400 亿美元 OpenAI 贷款，软银还单独寻求以其 OpenAI 股份作为担保的保证金贷款。

大部分义务不属于传统的债务披露范围。 研究表明，大型科技公司的表外人工智能承诺约为 1.65 万亿美元，仅 Meta 就占约 4200 亿美元，几乎是其报告债务的三倍。

OpenAI 从中得到什么

对于 OpenAI 来说，这笔交易将是迈向拥有其计算能力而不是从微软、亚马逊和甲骨文租用计算能力的第一步。 对基础设施的控制是谈判能力和命令能力之间的区别。

对于英伟达来说，计算的是需求确定性。 保证客户多年的芯片订单的稳定，否则客户将很难为其融资，这正是批评者认为这种安排令人不安的原因。

规模问题

今年人工智能基础设施支出将超过 7000 亿美元，预计到 2028 年该行业在数据中心上的支出将超过 3 万亿美元，其中大部分资金来自数据中心内部的芯片。 主要风险不是人工智能不起作用，而是扩建超出了需求，或者回报比债务摊销更快地被竞争消失。

什么也没有签署。 《华尔街日报》指出，有关该网站及其融资的谈判仍在进行中，并且可能会发生变化，这对于 2500 亿美元的担保来说是一个相当大的警告。
